entries.title: Proverbs 14:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Buildeth - Maintains and improves her family and estate. Her hands - By her idleness or sin.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A rod - His insolent speeches as they are like a rod, offensive to others, so, they make a rod for their own backs.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The crib - The stable is empty of food for cattle, and much more for man. In the same sense cleanness of teeth is put for famine, Amos 4:6 . The strength - By their labours, or by diligence in husbandry, which then was principally managed by oxen.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Findeth it not - Because he doth not seek it aright. That understandeth - That is honest and pious.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: His way - Consists not in vain speculations, but in a diligent study of his duty, and of the way to eternal happiness. The folly - The wit of ungodly men, which is really their folly, is employed only in finding out ways of deceiving.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Favour - They find favour both with God and men.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bitterness - The inward griefs and joys of mens hearts, are not known to any but a man's self.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Right - There are some evil courses which men may think to be lawful and good. The end - The event shews that they were sinful and destructive.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In laughter - The outward signs of joy are often mixed with real sorrow.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In heart - He who departs from God inwardly. Filled - With the fruit of his ways, the punishment of his sins. Satisfied - From the pious temper of his own heart, which cleaves to the Lord, he shall receive unspeakable comfort.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The simple - A foolish man. Looketh - He orders his dealings in the world with due circumspection, not considering so much what other men say as what he ought to do.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Feareth - Trembles at God's judgments when they are either inflicted or threatened. Rageth - Frets against God; or is enraged against his messengers. Confident - Secure and insensible of his danger.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Foolishly - His passion hurries him into foolish speeches and actions. Wicked devices - One who suppresses his passion, but meditates revenge. Hated - Both by God and men.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Inherit - They possess it as their inheritance, holding it fast, and glorying in it. Knowledge - The saving knowledge of God and of their own duty.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The evil - Good men shall have the pre - eminency over the wicked.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hated - Despised and abandoned.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Despiseth - That does not pity and relieve the poor.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The talk - Idle talking will bring a man to poverty.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Riches - They are a singular advantage and ornament to them. But - As for rich fools, their folly is not cured, but made worse and more manifest by their riches.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Souls - Such as are innocent, from false accusations.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To depart - To preserve men from destructive courses.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Exalteth - Heb. lifteth up, like a banner, makes it known and visible to all men.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:30
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A sound heart - Free from envy and inordinate passions. Is life - Procures and maintains the health and vigour of the body.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: His maker - Whose image the poor man bears, by whose providence he is made poor, and who hath declared himself to be their protector and avenger.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:32
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Driven away - In his death, from God's favour and presence. Death - In his greatest dangers and distresses, yea even in death itself.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:33
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Resteth - Is laid up and hid there. In the midst - In the heart. Made known - They will publish in all times and companies.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:35–15:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shame - Both to himself, by his foolish management of the king's affairs, and to the king who made so foolish a choice of a servant.
